product.olivetti-m4-452s.summary: The DX2 option in the M4-4xx Entry range, in a compact case with fewer expansion positions.
product.olivetti-m4-452s.history: In the mid-1990s, Olivetti combined different motherboards, 486 processors and cases to adapt a single computer line to different audiences. The M4-452 S Modulo belonged to Olivetti’s professional M4 Modulo range, positioned between the PCS machines for personal use and the M6 Suprema according to MCmicrocomputer 137 (February 1994, p. 176). Within the M4-4xx line it combined the Entry platform with the compact SLIM TIN BOX case; its alternative case version was the M4-452 Modulo. Olivetti’s guide distinguishes these commercial variants on p. 4-1 and their boards on pp. 4-2–6.
product.olivetti-m4-452s.warning: Candidate configuration. PDKK is confirmed on a physical BA2142. Its attribution to this commercial model is still pending.
product.olivetti-m4-452s.technical.ident: The case and board distinguish this configuration from its siblings. The manual identifies M4-452 S Modulo as KPS44 D50, with a Entry board, a 50 MHz CPU and a 25 MHz bus. In its table, S identifies the compact M4 case and E the large PCS42P case; E does not mean Entry.
product.olivetti-m4-452s.technical.memor: RAM expands through two modules. The guide supports 4–64 MB in two 70 ns SIMM banks: 4/8/16/32 MB modules with parity or 4/8 MB without parity, including mixed populations. It provides for 128 or 256 KB L2 cache; standard installation is not assumed.
product.olivetti-m4-452s.technical.slots: Case size determines how many cards fit. The IN2025 riser offers 3 positions: two shared ISA/VESA and 1 ISA; the motherboard also provides an AT connection for audio. The guide specifies a 100 W power supply (pp. 4-2–3).
product.olivetti-m4-452s.technical.flash: The BIOS can be updated from floppy disk. The manual lists revisions 1.09–1.11 and calls the 28F001BX ‘1 MB’ (pp. 4-7 and 4-10); Intel specifies 1 Mbit, 128K × 8, or 128 KiB (290406-007, p. 1). These are different units; retaining the manual’s wording does not endorse that capacity.
product.olivetti-m4-452s.technical.dump: The preserved dump from a physical BA2142 contains American Megatrends’ PDKK AMIBIOS (128 KiB). The photo shows an SMC FDC37C653, while Olivetti's guide specifies the 37C651 for Entry. The photographed IN2025 riser belongs to the compact case. This configuration fits that case, but the donor model remains unidentified. The 1.11 diagnostics string does not identify the commercial BIOS revision.
product.olivetti-m4-452s.technical.verif: In BluMach, the experimental BA2142 with PDKK and 486DX2/50 (25 MHz bus) saved the IDE geometry through the original Setup. After a power cycle, it booted Olivetti MS-DOS 5.00 from C: and read a file. It also booted from floppy.
product.olivetti-m4-452s.technical.limit: The tests cover the experimental board. This commercial model still needs a firmware match and validation of its storage configuration. BluMach uses a chipset approximation and an SMC37C651, with read-only flash.
product.olivetti-m4-452s.technical.sourc: Olivetti, Personal Computer — Pocket Service Guide, M4-4x4/M4-4x2/PCS42P chapter, pp. 4-1–7, 4-10 and 4-13: identity, architecture and revisions; discrepancies retained.
Paolo Ciardelli, ‘Olivetti M4-62 Modulo’, MCmicrocomputer 137, February 1994, p. 176: positioning of the M4, PCS and M6 ranges; the M4-62 price is not transferred.
Intel, 1-Mbit Boot Block Flash Memory, 290406-007, November 1995, p. 1: 28F001BX capacity; the date belongs to the document, not the computer.
BluMach 88f74ba3, machine_table.c and m_at_socket1.c: experimental BA2142 platform, code comparison without validation of this model.
product.olivetti-m4-452s.technical.board: Entry integrates video and disk control to leave expansion slots free. The guide specifies CL-GD5424 with 512 KB expandable to 1 MB and SMC37C651 for floppy and IDE. BA2142 derives from BA2148 Entry; that revision is not assigned to every unit. The 82C611 belongs to Enhanced (pp. 4-3 and 4-7). The guide lists 170, 210, 340, 420, 540 MB and 1 GB drives for the family (p. 4-2), without assigning them to this configuration.
